clue.text: With Sinuous Sue on toadstool, boy endlessly agog is very shy

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the word before it is dropped

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for with

indicators.note: something sinuous winds and twists, so the words it governs are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder
the word agog cut short by one letter

annotation.spelling: WOULDN'T SAY BOO TO A GOOSE

explanation.surface: A boy gazes wide-eyed at Sue, who is perched on a toadstool like a fairy-tale figure.
explanation.walkthrough: W for with leads, then everything from Sue to the clipped agog is rearranged into the rest of the idiom WOULDN'T SAY BOO TO A GOOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone so timid they would not even startle a harmless farmyard bird, so it describes a very shy person.

clue.text: Somewhat Conservative name Left must expel

indicators.note: expelling throws something out, so a letter is removed from the word for left

parts.note: left as in departed
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A party member with mild Tory views is someone the Left would want thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: In British politics a wet is a moderate Conservative, the name Mrs Thatcher's allies gave to those who opposed her harder policies.
explanation.definitionFit: Wet is the British political label for a moderate, lukewarm member of the Tory party, hence only somewhat Conservative.

clue.text: The German coming in brought to naught? That's rare

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: brought to ruin, undone
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A question about plans brought to nothing, answered with the remark that this seldom happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rare' reads like seldom in the surface, but here it describes meat cooked only lightly.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare meat is cooked very briefly, which is to say not cooked through, lightly done.

clue.text: Daughter with a friend regularly took on challenge

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
taken as written

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A daughter and her friend accepted a challenge together.
explanation.definitionFit: To dare is to have the courage to face something, so having dared means having accepted a challenge.

clue.text: Male astride little horse in New Forest for instance

indicators.note: a rider astride sits with legs either side, so one piece straddles the other

parts.note: a tom is a male animal, especially a cat
a pony is a small horse

explanation.surface: A man rides a pony through the New Forest, an English area famous for its wild ponies.
explanation.walkthrough: The New Forest is a region of southern England, a place name, hence an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A toponym is a place name, and New Forest is the name of a region in Hampshire, England.

clue.text: Dodgy meal in time brings complaint

indicators.note: dodgy means unsound or suspect, so the letters are not in their proper order

parts.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A suspect dinner eaten at some point leaves a diner with a grievance against the restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a complaint to a waiter; the answer is the medical sense of complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is an illness or disorder, which is what an ailment is.

clue.text: Luxurious hotel removed sign of the cross?

indicators.note: removed means taken away, so a letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: plush means luxurious
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A grand hotel has taken down its religious crucifix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sign of the cross' suggests a religious gesture, but the plus sign is a cross shape.
explanation.definitionFit: The plus symbol is drawn as a small upright cross, so it is literally a sign shaped like the cross.

clue.text: Fools seen in the French city

indicators.note: something seen in another is located inside it

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for the
has as in deceives, as in 'you've been had'

explanation.surface: Clowns spotted in some French city.
explanation.walkthrough: Fools looks like a plural noun but is a verb: to have someone is to trick them.
explanation.definitionFit: Lhasa is the capital city of Tibet, so it is a straightforward example of a city.

clue.text: Writing very quickly? Hey! Song part needs a rewrite!

indicators.note: a rewrite reworks the text, so these letters are put into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A songwriter scribbling fast exclaims that one section of the song must be redone.
explanation.definitionFit: Stenography is shorthand, a system of symbols that lets a writer record speech at great speed.

clue.text: Garment long that covers first-class behind

indicators.note: covering something means going around it, so one piece is wrapped round the rest

parts.note: to pine is to long or yearn
A as in A1, top quality
behind as in supporting, in favour of

explanation.surface: A long dress that covers a very fine backside.
explanation.walkthrough: Behind looks like a body part in the surface but means backing, as when you are behind a candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinafore is a sleeveless dress or apron worn over other clothes, a type of garment.

clue.text: Royal family study form, disregarding all outsiders

indicators.note: ignoring the outsiders means the outer letters of each word are dropped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Students of the monarchy fill in a form while ignoring anyone from outside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were the English royal dynasty from Henry VII to Elizabeth I.

clue.text: Beat friend hollow and scoffed

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a pit is a hollow
to scoff is to eat greedily

explanation.surface: Someone thrashed a friend soundly and jeered at them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat hollow' reads as a phrase for thrashing someone; the words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To palpitate is to throb or pulse rapidly, as a heart does, which is what beat means here.

clue.text: Dare maybe in northern clubs to enter undressed for social

indicators.note: in places one item inside the pair of letters around it
entering means going inside, so this group is put within the next word

parts.note: bare means unclothed
N is the abbreviation for northern
Dan Dare is a British comic-strip space hero, so Dan is an example of a Dare
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A dare to walk into northern nightclubs naked, all for the sake of socialising.
explanation.walkthrough: Dan Dare, Pilot of the Future, is a hero of the British comic Eagle; 'maybe' tells you Dare is a surname standing for its first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A social is an informal gathering, and a barn dance is a country-style party with folk dancing.

clue.text: See 1
Strike with fear losing right old battle

indicators.note: losing something means it is lost from the word, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: to alarm is to frighten
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An old battle in which the side in the right was terrified and defeated.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo was the 1836 siege in Texas, a famous battle of the Texas Revolution.

clue.text: Creature in love shortly after wrestling?

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the last letter is removed from each of the following words

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
post is a prefix meaning after
sumo is Japanese wrestling

explanation.surface: A creature falls in love not long after a bout of wrestling.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: this tree-climbing American marsupial is simply one kind of animal, and creature is the general word for any living beast.

clue.text: Phaeton's redesigned as one-seater carriage

indicators.note: a redesign changes the arrangement, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A phaeton, a light horse-drawn carriage, is rebuilt so that only one person can sit in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanhope is a light open horse-drawn gig with a single seat, named after an English clergyman.

clue.text: Revolutionary socialist cause in As You Like It?

indicators.note: a revolution turns something around, so the following words are read backwards

parts.note: a red is a socialist
the root of something is its cause

explanation.surface: A question about whether a left-wing political cause features in Shakespeare's comedy As You Like It.
explanation.walkthrough: The title of Shakespeare's play is reread as a plain phrase: made as you like it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made to order is made to the customer's specification, exactly as they like it.

clue.text: Dusky fellow, Scotsman from Tayside city

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour
a don is a fellow of a university college
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A dark-haired man described as a Scot from a city on the River Tay.
explanation.walkthrough: Dundee is the city on the Firth of Tay in eastern Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dundonian is a native of Dundee, the principal city of the Tayside region of Scotland.

clue.text: Cow up by Scottish loch

parts.note: up as in finished: time is up, it is over
Loch Awe is a large loch in Argyll

explanation.surface: A cow standing beside a Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Cow looks like the animal, but it is the verb meaning to intimidate.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to intimidate them into submission, just as to overawe is to subdue by impressiveness.

clue.text: Leaderless coppers seizing throne in Vatican City?

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold, so the outer piece closes around the inner one
without a leader means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: coppers are low-value copper coins, pennies
the throne is jokey slang for the toilet, a lav

explanation.surface: Police without their chief storm the papal throne in the Vatican.
explanation.walkthrough: Coppers suggests police, but means coins; throne suggests the papal seat, but is slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Vatican City is a sovereign state wholly surrounded by Rome, an example of a territory enclosed within another.

clue.text: Footie tournament with investment of bank: make killing

indicators.note: to invest is to clothe or surround, so one piece is wrapped in the other

parts.note: a cup competition in football
to bank is to tilt or lean, as an aircraft does

explanation.surface: A football tournament backed by a bank's investment turns a big profit.
explanation.walkthrough: Investment and bank point to finance, but invest means to surround and bank means tilt; footie is British slang for football.
explanation.definitionFit: To clean up is an idiom for winning or earning a great deal of money, as does making a killing.

clue.text: Sophist from Civil Service touring ace Hebridean islands

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the outer piece travels around the inner

parts.note: CS is the abbreviation for Civil Service
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards
North and South Uist are islands of the Outer Hebrides

explanation.surface: A smooth-talking civil servant goes on a tour of the Scottish isles with a top colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: A casuist reasons cleverly but speciously, especially on moral questions, just like a sophist.

clue.text: Waist measurement potentially right

indicators.note: potentially means it could become something else, so these letters may be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tailor's measurement around the waist might be correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Girth is the distance around something, and the girth around the middle is a waist measurement.

clue.text: Marley was one coming in for a start

indicators.note: coming in points inside the following words, where the letters sit unbroken

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: Bob Marley was one of the first to arrive, a newcomer at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Marley, the reggae musician, was a famous follower of the Rastafarian movement.

clue.text: Cat just after occupying snug offers universal theory

indicators.note: occupying a space means being inside it, so these pieces go within the next word

on as in 'on the hour', immediately after

explanation.definitionFit: Cosmogony is the study or theory of how the universe originated.

clue.text: Final letter from duck sitting on mammoth

parts.note: a duck is a score of zero in cricket, shaped like O
mega means huge

explanation.surface: A last message received from a duck perched on a woolly mammoth.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, hence a final letter.

clue.text: Where fare goes down, Iago hopes, when travelling

indicators.note: travelling means moving about, so the letters move out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Iago, the schemer from Othello, wonders where his bus fare will end up on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: Fare suggests a ticket price, but it is food, which goes down the gullet.
explanation.definitionFit: The oesophagus is the gullet, the tube carrying food from throat to stomach; this is its plural.

clue.text: 100 seen in backing current decree

indicators.note: going backwards means the word is read from end to start
seen in places this item inside the other

parts.note: a tide is a current of water
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A hundred people are seen supporting the latest official order.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an official order issued by an authority, which is what a decree is.

clue.text: Rise of Little Dorothy Fox

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: Dot is a short form of the name Dorothy

explanation.surface: The rise of a little girl called Dorothy, named Fox.
explanation.definitionFit: Tod is an old and dialect word for a fox, especially used in Scotland and northern England.

clue.text: Antelope minus tail in dash

indicators.note: without its tail means the last letter is chopped off

parts.note: an eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: A tailless antelope makes a dash for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan means vigour and style, the same flair as dash.

clue.text: Came down after siesta, subdued

indicators.note: after means coming later, so the first-named piece is placed second

parts.note: a siesta is an afternoon rest
rain comes down

explanation.surface: Rain fell after the afternoon nap, and everyone was in a quiet mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Restrained means held back and quiet, matching the muted sense of subdued.
